key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky imagery with RMSE close to a full-dataset ViT baseline.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly irradiance instrumentation for photovoltaic performance optimisation and solar energy forecasting.
method: Add calculated extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time features.
Use predicted global horizontal irradiance to refine diffuse irradiance estimates in a sequential pipeline.
Process raw and cloud-overlay sky images in parallel, using unsupervised, physics-informed segmentation.
evidence_signal: At Chilbolton Observatory, single-month training and temporally disjoint full-year testing yielded RMSE within 2–3 W/m² for the sequential framework and 1–6 W/m² for the dual-parallel framework relative to a full-dataset ViT.
watch_item: Validation at one temperate-climate site leaves generalisation to other climates and imaging setups unestablished.
paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
